result.note: Tests the CBFC leadership change, its term and predecessors, the Padma Shri's rank, and the ministry behind Prasar Bharati appointments; the Jana Nayagan row is left as context.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the leadership of the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) as of May 2026:
items: Shashi Shekhar Vempati was appointed CBFC chairperson for a three-year term.
Prasoon Joshi had led the CBFC since August 2017, succeeding Pahlaj Nihalani.
Vempati received the Padma Shri, India's third-highest civilian honour, in January 2026.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong because the Padma Shri is India's fourth-highest civilian honour, not the third. Vempati, a former CEO of Rajya Sabha TV and Prasar Bharati, replaced Joshi, whose tenure focused on digitising the board's certification process.
questions.source: He previously served as CEO of Rajya Sabha TV and Prasar Bharati, and received a Padma Shri, India’s fourth-highest civilian honour, in January 2026.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, Prasoon Joshi was moved from the Central Board of Film Certification to head Prasar Bharati, India's public broadcaster. Which ministry made this move?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
questions.explain: The Information and Broadcasting Ministry moved Joshi to Prasar Bharati on 2 May 2026, creating the CBFC vacancy that Vempati filled. The two men have effectively traded chairs across the same two institutions.
questions.source: On May 2, the Information and Broadcasting (I&B) Ministry moved him to head Prasar Bharati, creating the vacancy Vempati now fills.
